candidates.source_name: OCP Data Registry — Kosovo: Public Procurement Regulatory Commission (PPRC) publication
candidates.why_relevant: Registry entry describing Kosovo's OCDS publication: points to the PPRC OCDS API, bulk JSON/Excel/CSV downloads by year back to March 2016, OCID prefix ocds-uhzcmx, and documents known data-quality traps (awards array misspelled as 'award', nulls, non-standard procuringEntity placement, Lots extension field typos). This is the single best map of how to get Kosovo procurement notices as structured data rather than scraping the portal.

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the registry page to resolve the current bulk-download and API endpoints, then pull yearly OCDS JSON dumps on a monthly cadence; normalise with an OCDS parser tolerant of the documented typos.

negative_findings.description: No aggregator or open-contracting dataset was found that is scoped specifically to banking, payments, cards, POS or ATM procurement in Kosovo.
negative_findings.result_summary: Every aggregator located is generalist (all-sector) and must be filtered by CPV code or keyword. Searching explicitly for banking/ATM/card tender aggregation for Kosovo returned only generic country pages and IFI portals.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must own the sector filtering layer (CPV + Albanian/Serbian keyword lists); no vendor supplies a ready-made banking-sector Kosovo feed.

negative_findings.description: Kosovo's OCDS publication has documented structural gaps and a stale quality review.
negative_findings.result_summary: The OCP registry entry reports ~211k parties and ~75.7k tenders but zero counts for awards, contracts and planning; the awards array is misspelled 'award'; procuringEntity sits in a non-standard location; Lots extension fields have typos; last quality review November 2021.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Award-notice coverage — the part that reveals who actually won banking/IT contracts — cannot be assumed present in the OCDS feed alone; a second source (Integrity Watch, Prokurimi i Hapur, or the portal itself) is required for awards.

negative_findings.description: Prokurimi i Hapur may not be refreshing.
negative_findings.result_summary: The site states data is currently being updated through the API system and asks users to report errors; the most recent update date observed on the page was 27 April 2023.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If the portal is frozen, it remains valuable as a historical archive but cannot serve as a live monitoring feed. Needs a liveness check before it is wired into a pipeline.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language aggregator coverage of Kosovo is thin and politically framed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Serbian-language searching surfaced only one aggregator with a real Kosovo section (javne-nabavke.com) plus a regional player (eKapija) whose stated coverage is BiH/Serbia/Montenegro. The Kosovo page's top-buyer list leads with a Serbia-administered provisional municipal body, indicating partial rather than national coverage.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Serbian-language collection cannot be relied on for full Kosovo coverage; sq and en remain the primary languages, with sr used mainly for Serb-majority municipality and cross-border angles.

negative_findings.description: dgMarket was referenced as a procurement aggregator but no Kosovo-specific dgMarket endpoint was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search results mentioned dgMarket only second-hand via a donor page; no dgMarket Kosovo country URL was reached in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: dgMarket historically aggregated World Bank/donor notices; if still active it would fill the IFI channel. Should be re-checked directly rather than recorded as absent.

negative_findings.description: Several commercial aggregators' Kosovo coverage depth could not be measured without a paid subscription.
negative_findings.result_summary: TendersInfo, GlobalTenders, TenderImpulse, TendersGo and TendersOnTime all advertise Kosovo coverage, but the actual notice count, latency and whether they carry award notices is behind a paywall/registration wall.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Their marketing claims must not be recorded as verified coverage; a trial-based bake-off against the OCDS feed is needed before any is paid for.

coverage_gaps.description: No single confirmed aggregator or dataset reliably carries Kosovo contract AWARD notices in structured form, given the zero award counts reported for the OCDS publication.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Triangulate awards across Integrity Watch Kosovo's procurement export, Prokurimi i Hapur's contract records and the PPRC portal itself; measure overlap before choosing a primary.

coverage_gaps.description: Commercial bank and PSP tenders (the buyers that matter most for a payments vendor) are private-sector RFPs largely outside public procurement portals; only press-scraping aggregators such as NjoftimePublike claim to capture them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated pass over Albanian press notice aggregators and bank websites' 'ftesë për ofertë / njoftim për tender' pages; this is arguably a separate cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Serbian-language (sr) aggregator coverage of Kosovo procurement was found to be shallow and only one genuine Kosovo-scoped section was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend sr-language searching to Serb-majority municipality bodies and Cyrillic-script variants ('јавне набавке', 'тендери', 'Косово'), and test whether javne-nabavke.com's Kosovo feed covers the whole territory.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI/donor procurement (EBRD ecepp, World Bank, KfW, EIB) covering Kosovo financial-sector and digital projects was only partially mapped in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicate a follow-up pass to ecepp.ebrd.com, World Bank procurement notices and EIB/KfW channels, filtered on Kosovo.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed archive strategy exists for notices that expire and vanish from e-prokurimi before an OCDS snapshot captures them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test TenderImpulse's dated archive URLs and the OCP yearly bulk files against a known set of expired Kosovo notices to quantify loss; consider own daily snapshotting.

coverage_gaps.description: None of the URLs in this slice were liveness-verified, and two (Prokurimi i Hapur freshness, the PPRC OCDS API endpoint) carry specific doubt.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic verification pass over all candidate URLs; treat any 403/timeout as bot-defence rather than death.

brief: Kosovo procurement aggregation has an unusually strong open-data spine for the region: the PPRC/KRPP publishes OCDS via an API with yearly JSON/Excel/CSV bulk files, catalogued and quality-annotated by the OCP Data Registry, and mirrored in part on the national opendata.rks-gov.net portal. Around it sits a dense NGO layer — Integrity Watch Kosovo (KDI/TI, with CSV/XLS/JSON procurement exports and conflict-of-interest red flags), Prokurimi i Hapur (Lëvizja FOL, trilingual sq/en/sr, possibly stale since 2023) and the regional Balkan Tender Watch coalition — which doubles as the best actor map for the sector. Commercial coverage splits by language: Albanian bid-alert services (Utender.eu, NjoftimePublike, VagonApp) are the local-market layer, a Serbian aggregator (javne-nabavke.com) offers the only real sr-language Kosovo section, and generalist global platforms (TendersInfo, GlobalTenders, TenderImpulse, TendersOnTime) add English normalisation and dated archives but unverifiable depth behind paywalls. The two structural blind spots are award notices — the OCDS publication reports zero awards, contracts and planning — and private-sector bank/PSP RFPs, neither of which any aggregator found here reliably covers.
